summary: Iteration 5: full backend regression + new strict email-OTP verification suite, plus frontend E2E of the register -> verify-otp -> login gating flow. Backend: 68/68 pytest tests pass (45 pre-existing regression tests adapted to the new no-auto-login register, + 23 new OTP tests in /app/backend/tests/test_otp_verification.py). Verified: register creates user with email_verified=false and returns HTTP 400 with 'Resend is not configured' + 'RESEND_API_KEY' (no auth cookies, user row persisted); duplicate verified email -> 400 'Email already registered'; existing UNVERIFIED email re-register updates password/name (not blocked); login for unverified user -> 403 with structured detail {code:'email_not_verified', email:...}; admin login still 200 with email_verified=true; verify-otp bad code -> 400 'Incorrect code' + attempts++ , 5 wrong attempts then 429 'Too many attempts' + OTP doc deleted, expired OTP -> 400 'expired' + deleted, no OTP -> 400 'No verification code pending', non-6-digit -> 400, correct seeded code -> 200 with email_verified=true + HttpOnly access/refresh cookies + OTP consumed + subsequent login allowed, OTP with no user -> 404; resend-otp: unknown email -> {ok:true} (no enumeration), verified email -> 400 'already verified', unverified -> 400 'Resend is not configured', within 60s of register -> 429 'Please wait Xs'; db.otps stores bcrypt code_hash ($2b$) with no plaintext 'code' field, expires_at is a BSON date, unique index on email + TTL index expireAfterSeconds=0 on expires_at both present; Google/emergent-session code path sets email_verified=true on both create and update (bogus session_id returns non-500). Regression: services/bookings/payments (Razorpay placeholder 400 + HMAC verify/webhook)/admin/contact all pass. Frontend: unverified login correctly redirects to /verify-otp?email=..., 6-digit input auto-advance, backspace navigation, non-numeric rejection and 6-digit paste all work, wrong code shows 'Incorrect code' toast and clears inputs, resend shows 'Please wait Xs' and starts the button cooldown, back link -> /register, /verify-otp without ?email redirects to /register, admin login -> /admin dashboard renders.

minor.issue: Error detail leaks internal configuration to end users: 'Account created but we couldn't send the verification email: Resend is not configured. Set RESEND_API_KEY in backend/.env (get one at https://resend.com/api-keys).' This string is rendered verbatim in a user-facing toast. Log the operator detail server-side and return a generic user message (e.g. 'We couldn't send the verification email. Please try again shortly.').

Re-registering an existing UNVERIFIED email within the 60s OTP cooldown returns 429 AFTER the password/name have already been overwritten in db.users. The write is not rolled back, so the client sees a failure while credentials silently changed. Consider issuing the OTP before mutating the user, or returning 200 with a 'cooldown' flag.

OTP doc (and therefore the 60s cooldown) is upserted BEFORE send_otp_email succeeds. When sending fails the user is locked out of /auth/resend-otp for 60s even though no email ever went out. Only start the cooldown after a successful send.

integration_issues.issue: With the placeholder Resend key the backend returns 400, so Register.jsx's catch block fires: the user stays on /register with a raw config-error toast and is NEVER navigated to /verify-otp, even though the account WAS created (email_verified=false). Re-submitting the same email then returns 429 'Please wait 60s'. The only escape is to go to /login and get the 403 redirect. Handle the 'account created but email send failed' case explicitly (e.g. backend returns 200 with {verification_required:true, email_sent:false}, or frontend navigates to /verify-otp when the 400 detail indicates the account was created).

issues: Long error toasts render over the Navbar and cover the 'Get Started'/'Logout' button in the top-right; consider bottom-right placement or shorter messages.

action_items: Decide the UX for 'account created but OTP email could not be sent': either return 200 with email_sent:false and let Register.jsx navigate to /verify-otp, or have Register.jsx navigate on that specific 400. Today the user is dead-ended on /register.
Stop returning internal .env/RESEND_API_KEY guidance in user-facing error details (register + resend-otp); log it instead.
Start the 60s OTP cooldown only after a successful Resend send, and don't mutate the user's password before the OTP is issued.
Split /app/backend/server.py (724 lines) and move the inline `__import__("pydantic").BaseModel` request models (VerifyOtpRequest, ResendOtpRequest, RazorpayVerifyRequest) into models.py.
Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: test1@labos.dev is now UNVERIFIED (login returns 403); document the OTP endpoints and the seed-OTP-in-db.otps pattern.
critical_code_review_comments: verify_otp: attempts are checked before the code comparison, so the 6th request (not the 5th failure) returns 429 — the documented behaviour holds, but the OTP stays usable until that extra call; deleting it as soon as attempts hits OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS would be tighter.
email_service.send_otp_email raises RuntimeError for the placeholder key and server.py maps it to 400 correctly (no 500/502) — verified end-to-end.
db.otps has a unique index on email, so one pending OTP per address; verify-otp deletes on success/expiry/lockout — no leak of stale codes observed.

login blocks unverified users but /auth/refresh and /auth/me do not re-check email_verified; currently unreachable (cookies are only issued post-verification), but an admin-driven un-verification would not revoke live sessions.
server.py is 724 lines (>700) — split auth/payments/admin routers into modules.

success_rate.frontend: 90% — all OTP UI mechanics and login gating pass; register->verify-otp navigation blocked by the 400 handling

seed_data_creation: Suite registers throwaway test_*@labos.dev users (deleted in fixture teardown for the OTP module), seeds bcrypt-hashed OTPs directly into db.otps, and seeds/removes payment_transactions. backend_test.py now marks its client fixture verified directly in Mongo (make_verified_client helper) since register no longer logs in.
test_credentials: admin@labos.tech / Labos@2026 (admin, auto-verified). test1@labos.dev / Test@1234 is now UNVERIFIED -> login returns 403 email_not_verified (confirmed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: OTP tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_otp_verification.py; positive verify path uses seed_otp() which writes a bcrypt code_hash straight into db.otps. backend_test.py gained make_verified_client() — register returns 400 with the placeholder Resend key, so the helper flips email_verified in Mongo and then logs in. If real RESEND_API_KEY is ever added, every assertion expecting 400 'Resend is not configured' (register/resend tests) must flip to 200. Frontend register cannot reach /verify-otp while the Resend key is a placeholder; use /login with an unverified user to land on the verify page.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect in the OTP logic itself. The one user-visible gap is a contract mismatch: /auth/register raises 400 when the OTP email fails, but Register.jsx only navigates to /verify-otp on success, so with the placeholder Resend key the freshly-created (unverified) account has no in-app path to verification and the raw 'Set RESEND_API_KEY in backend/.env' string is shown to the end user. Secondary: the OTP doc + 60s cooldown are persisted before the send attempt, so a failed send still blocks resend for 60s.
